literal_meaning: A city of darkness, a senseless king.
figurative_meaning: Complete disorder due to incompetent leadership.
example: Is daftar mein koi niyam nahi hai — andheri nagari chaupat raja.

idiom: आसमान से गिरा खजूर में अटका
literal_meaning: Fell from the sky, got stuck in the date-palm.
figurative_meaning: Escaping one problem only to land in another.
example: Ek musibat se nikla toh doosri aa gayi — asmaan se gira khajoor mein atka.

literal_meaning: A cumin seed in a camel's mouth.
figurative_meaning: A completely insufficient amount for a large need.
example: Itne kaam ke liye sirf do log — yeh toh unt ke munh mein jeera hai.

literal_meaning: The insider's informer destroys Lanka.
figurative_meaning: Betrayal from within causes the greatest damage.
example: Data leak andar wale ne kiya — ghar ka bhedi Lanka dhaye.

literal_meaning: Can't dance, blames the crooked courtyard.
figurative_meaning: Blaming external factors for one's own incompetence.
example: Ravi haar gaya aur pitch ko dosh diya — naach na jaane aangan tedha.

idiom: दूध का दूध पानी का पानी
literal_meaning: Milk is milk, water is water.
figurative_meaning: To deliver a perfectly fair and clear judgment.
example: Judge ne sach saaf kar diya — doodh ka doodh paani ka paani.

literal_meaning: One path, two tasks.
figurative_meaning: Accomplishing two things with a single effort.
example: Delhi mein kaam bhi hua aur dost se bhi mila — ek panth do kaaj.

idiom: जल में रहकर मगर से बैर
literal_meaning: Enmity with the crocodile while living in water.
figurative_meaning: Picking a fight with someone you depend on.
example: Boss se hi dushman mol li — jal mein rahkar magar se bair.

literal_meaning: An empty chickpea makes the most noise.
figurative_meaning: Those with little knowledge or substance make the most noise.
example: Woh sirf baatein karta hai, kaam kuch nahi — thotha chana baje ghana.

idiom: बंदर क्या जाने अदरक का स्वाद
literal_meaning: What does a monkey know of the taste of ginger?
figurative_meaning: A person cannot appreciate something beyond their understanding.
example: Use art ki koi samajh nahi — bandar kya jaane adrak ka swad.

idiom: लातों के भूत बातों से नहीं मानते
literal_meaning: Ghosts of kicks don't listen to words.
figurative_meaning: Some people only respond to force, not reason.
example: Usne samjhane par dhyan nahi diya — laaton ke bhoot baaton se nahi maante.

literal_meaning: A half-filled pot keeps spilling.
figurative_meaning: People with little knowledge tend to show off the most.
example: Naye student hi sabse zyada bolte hain — adhajal gagri chhalkat jaye.

literal_meaning: Black letters are equal to a buffalo.
figurative_meaning: Completely illiterate or unable to understand something.
example: Unhe contract padh ke kuch samajh nahi aaya — kala akshar bhains barabar.

literal_meaning: A straw in the thief's beard.
figurative_meaning: A guilty person always feels suspicious and exposed.
example: Jab naam liya toh woh ghabra gaya — chor ki dadhi mein tinka.

literal_meaning: Keeping a foot on two boats.
figurative_meaning: Trying to pursue two conflicting paths simultaneously.
example: Woh naukri bhi karna chahta hai aur padhai bhi — do naavon par pair rakhna.

idiom: मन चंगा तो कठौती में गंगा
literal_meaning: If the heart is pure, the Ganga is in the washbasin.
figurative_meaning: A pure mind finds the divine everywhere; inner purity matters more than ritual.
example: Zaruri nahi mandir jao — man changa toh kathauti mein Ganga.

idiom: साँप भी मर जाए और लाठी भी न टूटे
literal_meaning: The snake dies and the stick doesn't break either.
figurative_meaning: Achieving the goal without losing or sacrificing anything.
example: Usne jhagda sुलझाया aur dono खुश रहे — saanp bhi mar jaye aur laathi bhi na toote.

idiom: अपनी गली में कुत्ता भी शेर होता है
literal_meaning: Even a dog is a lion in its own lane.
figurative_meaning: People feel bold and brave only in their own familiar territory.
example: Woh apne gaon mein bahut brave hai — apni gali mein kutta bhi sher hota hai.

literal_meaning: Dug a mountain, out came a mouse.
figurative_meaning: Great effort or expectation resulting in a very small outcome.
example: Itni mehnat ke baad sirf yeh result — khoda pahad nikli chuhiya.

literal_meaning: Why does a bracelet on the hand need a mirror?
figurative_meaning: An obvious truth needs no further proof.
example: Woh cheater hai, sab dekh chuke hain — haath kangan ko aarsi kya.

literal_meaning: As the country, so the dress.
figurative_meaning: One should adapt to the customs and norms of wherever they are.
example: Yahan ka tarika seekh lo — jaisa desh waisa bhesh.

literal_meaning: The thief reprimands the police officer.
figurative_meaning: The wrongdoer blames or attacks the person trying to hold them accountable.
example: Usne galti ki aur mujhe hi daant raha hai — ulta chor kotwal ko daante.

idiom: अब पछताए होत क्या जब चिड़िया चुग गई खेत
literal_meaning: What use is regret when the bird has already eaten the field?
figurative_meaning: Regret is useless after the damage is already done.
example: Exam ke baad padhne baitha — ab pachtaye hot kya jab chidiya chug gayi khet.

literal_meaning: Nine plus two equals eleven.
figurative_meaning: To flee or escape quickly.
example: Police dekhi toh woh nau do gyarah ho gaya.

literal_meaning: Washing one's hands in the flowing Ganga.
figurative_meaning: Taking advantage of an opportunity while it lasts.
example: Sab profit le rahe the toh usne bhi liya — behti Ganga mein haath dhona.

literal_meaning: Blind in the eyes, named Nayansukh (joy of eyes).
figurative_meaning: A person whose name or reputation is the complete opposite of reality.
example: Woh manager hai par kuch manage nahi karta — aankh ka andha naam Nayansukh.

idiom: कहाँ राजा भोज कहाँ गंगू तेली
literal_meaning: Where is King Bhoj and where is Gangu the oil-presser?
figurative_meaning: A huge gap between two people in status, ability, or class.
example: Uski tulna us expert se mat karo — kahan raja Bhoj kahan Gangu teli.

literal_meaning: Whoever has the stick owns the buffalo.
figurative_meaning: Power belongs to those who are strongest; might is right.
example: Wahan jo powerful hai woh rules banata hai — jiski laathi uski bhains.

idiom: सौ सुनार की एक लुहार की
literal_meaning: One blow of a blacksmith equals a hundred of a goldsmith.
figurative_meaning: One decisive action is worth more than a hundred small or weak ones.
example: Usne ek baar mein kaam khatam kar diya — sau sunaar ki ek luhaar ki.

idiom: मुँह में राम बगल में छुरी
literal_meaning: Ram's name on the lips, a knife under the arm.
figurative_meaning: Someone who appears pious or friendly but harbors deceitful intentions.
example: Woh meetha bolta hai par daga deta hai — munh mein Ram bagal mein churi.

idiom: अकेला चना भाड़ नहीं फोड़ सकता
literal_meaning: A single chickpea cannot burst the roaster.
figurative_meaning: One person alone cannot bring about major change.
example: Ek insaan se yeh system nahi badlega — akela chana bhaad nahi phod sakta.

idiom: घर का जोगी जोगड़ा आन गाँव का सिद्ध
literal_meaning: The ascetic at home is ordinary; the one from another village is revered.
figurative_meaning: Familiarity breeds contempt; outsiders are valued more than locals.
example: Apne teacher ko ignore karte hain, bahar wale ko mante hain — ghar ka jogi jogda.

idiom: आम के आम गुठलियों के दам
literal_meaning: The mango itself and profit from its seeds too.
figurative_meaning: Getting double benefit from a single thing.
example: Kaam bhi hua aur paise bhi mile — aam ke aam guthlion ke daam.

literal_meaning: Do good and throw it in the river.
figurative_meaning: Do good deeds without expecting anything in return.
example: Usne madad ki aur bhool gaya — neki kar dariya mein daal.

idiom: पानी में रहकर मगरमच्छ से बैर नहीं
literal_meaning: Don't make an enemy of the crocodile while living in water.
figurative_meaning: Avoid conflict with those who have power over you.
example: Office mein manager se mat lado — paani mein rahkar magarmacch se bair nahi.

idiom: जब तक साँस तब तक आस
literal_meaning: As long as there is breath, there is hope.
figurative_meaning: One should never give up hope while alive.
example: Haaro mat — jab tak saans tab tak aas.

idiom: चार दिन की चाँदनी फिर अँधेरी रात
literal_meaning: Four days of moonlight, then a dark night.
figurative_meaning: Good times don't last forever.
example: Yeh khushi zyada din nahi chalegi — chaar din ki chandni phir andheri raat.

literal_meaning: Even a fleeing ghost's loincloth is valuable.
figurative_meaning: Something is better than nothing.
example: Thoda paisa hi sahi, kuch toh mila — bhagate bhoot ki langoti bhali.

idiom: दूर के ढोल सुहावने लगते हैं
literal_meaning: Drums from afar sound pleasant.
figurative_meaning: Things appear better from a distance than they really are.
example: Woh desh bahut acha lagta hai par rehna mushkil hai — door ke dhol suhawne lagte hain.

idiom: बिन माँगे मोती मिले माँगे मिले न भीख
literal_meaning: Pearls come unasked; begging yields nothing.
figurative_meaning: Fate gives freely what it will; begging or demanding gets you nothing.
example: Jab expect nahi kiya tab promotion mila — bin maange moti mile.

literal_meaning: Eyes become four.
figurative_meaning: To meet face to face; also to fall in love.
example: Pehli baar jab unse mila toh aankhen char ho gayin.

literal_meaning: A frog in a well.
figurative_meaning: A person with a very limited worldview and no exposure to the wider world.
example: Usne kabhi shehar nahi dekha — woh kuen ka mendhak hai.

literal_meaning: No sooner was the head shaved than hailstones fell.
figurative_meaning: Bad luck strikes right at the start of a new venture.
example: Dukaan kholi aur pehle din hi market crash ho gayi — sir mundaate hi ole pade.

idiom: एक हाथ से ताली नहीं बजती
literal_meaning: A clap cannot be made with one hand.
figurative_meaning: No conflict or cooperation happens without both sides participating.
example: Dono ki galti hai — ek haath se taali nahi bajti.

idiom: मन के हारे हार है मन के जीते जीत
literal_meaning: Defeated in mind is defeat; victorious in mind is victory.
figurative_meaning: The outcome depends on your mental attitude and willpower.
example: Himmat rakho — man ke haare haar hai man ke jeete jeet.

literal_meaning: First come, first served.
figurative_meaning: Those who act early get the benefit.
example: Tickets sirf pehle sau logon ko milenge — pehle aao pehle pao.

literal_meaning: As you sow, so shall you reap.
figurative_meaning: Your actions determine your consequences.
example: Usne dhooka diya aur ab khud taklif mein hai — jaisi karni waisi bharni.

idiom: काम का न काज का दुश्मन अनाज का
literal_meaning: Of no use for work or task, but an enemy of grain (a freeloader).
figurative_meaning: A person who is completely useless but consumes resources.
example: Woh kuch nahi karta sirf khaata hai — kaam ka na kaaj ka dushman anaaj ka.

idiom: हाथी के दाँत खाने के और दिखाने के और
literal_meaning: An elephant has different teeth for eating and for showing.
figurative_meaning: Saying one thing publicly and doing something else privately; hypocrisy.
example: Woh sab ke saamne seedha banta hai par andar se alag hai — haathi ke daant.

literal_meaning: Remembering one's maternal grandmother.
figurative_meaning: To be in great distress or difficulty.
example: Itna kaam dekha toh nani yaad aa gayi.

literal_meaning: When caution leaves, accidents happen.
figurative_meaning: A moment of carelessness is all it takes for disaster to strike.
example: Ek pal dhyan hata aur haath cut gaya — saavdhaani hati durghatna ghati.

literal_meaning: Stretch your legs only as far as the blanket reaches.
figurative_meaning: Live within your means; don't spend beyond what you have.
example: Itna udhar mat lo — chadar dekhkar pair phailao.

idiom: जो गरजते हैं वो बरसते नहीं
literal_meaning: Those who thunder do not rain.
figurative_meaning: People who make the most noise rarely follow through with action.
example: Vaoh bahut dhamki deta hai par kuch karta nahi — jo garajte hain wo barsate nahi.

idiom: हर चमकने वाली चीज़ सोना नहीं होती
literal_meaning: Not everything that shines is gold.
figurative_meaning: Appearances can be deceptive; not everything attractive is valuable.
example: Woh company bahut achi lagti thi par andar khaali thi — har chamakne wali cheez sona nahi hoti.

literal_meaning: An empty mind is the devil's house.
figurative_meaning: Idle people tend to get into trouble or think harmful thoughts.
example: Kuch karo, baithhe rehne se bura sochte ho — khaali dimaag shaitan ka ghar.

literal_meaning: Grass does not grow on stone.
figurative_meaning: A hard-hearted person cannot be made compassionate.
example: Use samjhana bekar hai — patthar par doob nahi jamti.

idiom: तेली का तेल जले, मशालची का दिल जले
literal_meaning: The oil-seller's oil burns, the torchbearer's heart burns.
figurative_meaning: Someone else does the work and bears the cost, while another person takes the credit or glory.
example: Main kaam karta hoon, woh naam leta hai — teli ka tel jale, mashalchi ka dil jale.

idiom: बोया पेड़ बबूल का आम कहाँ से होय
literal_meaning: You planted a thorn tree, where will mangoes come from?
figurative_meaning: You cannot expect good results from bad actions.
example: Usne dhoka diya aur ab wafadaari chahta hai — boya ped babul ka aam kahan se hoy.

literal_meaning: Straightening one's own owl.
figurative_meaning: To serve only one's own selfish interests.
example: Woh kisi ki madad nahi karta, apna ullu seedha karta hai.

idiom: कभी नाव गाड़ी पर कभी गाड़ी नाव पर
literal_meaning: Sometimes the boat rides the cart, sometimes the cart rides the boat.
figurative_meaning: Life is unpredictable; roles and circumstances keep reversing.
example: Aaj woh bada hai, kal hum the — kabhi naav gaadi par kabhi gaadi naav par.

literal_meaning: Doing good and asking about it repeatedly.
figurative_meaning: True kindness needs no announcement; advertising generosity defeats its purpose.
example: Usne donate kiya aur sab ko bataya — neki aur pooch pooch.

literal_meaning: Truth is bitter.
figurative_meaning: Honest words are often unpleasant but necessary.
example: Mujhe pata tha woh nahi sunenge — sachhai kadvi hoti hai.

literal_meaning: You drink the water and then ask about the caste.
figurative_meaning: Raising irrelevant objections only after already benefiting from something.
example: Kaam karwa liya, ab zyada sawaal — paani peekar jaat poochte ho.

literal_meaning: What use is regret after the hand is cut?
figurative_meaning: Regretting after the damage is done is useless.
example: Ab rona kyun — haath kate baad pachtava kya.

idiom: उस पार की घास हरी होती है
literal_meaning: The grass on the other side is green.
figurative_meaning: What others have always seems better than what you have.
example: Woh desh acha lagta hai — us paar ki ghaas hari hoti hai.

idiom: बिल्ली के भाग्य से छींका टूटा
literal_meaning: By the cat's luck the shelf broke.
figurative_meaning: Getting something by sheer luck rather than effort or deserve.
example: Usse chance achanch mil gaya — billi ke bhagya se chhika toota.

idiom: रस्सी जल गई पर ऐंठ न गई
literal_meaning: The rope burned but the twist didn't leave it.
figurative_meaning: Even after losing everything, the arrogant person does not give up their pride.
example: Sab kho diya phir bhi ghamand hai — rassi jal gayi par aintha na gayi.

literal_meaning: Many are skilled at giving advice to others.
figurative_meaning: People are quick to advise others but rarely follow their own counsel.
example: Woh mujhe batata hai par khud nahi karta — par updesh kushal bahutere.

literal_meaning: Borax on gold.
figurative_meaning: Something that adds extra value to something already excellent.
example: Ache project mein uski help bhi mil gayi — sone par suhaga.

idiom: काम का समय काम करो, खेल का समय खेलो
literal_meaning: Work at work time, play at play time.
figurative_meaning: There is a right time for everything; don't mix responsibilities with leisure.
example: Office mein timepass mat karo — kaam ka samay kaam karo khel ka samay khelo.

literal_meaning: Incomplete knowledge is dangerous.
figurative_meaning: Partial understanding of something can cause more harm than total ignorance.
example: Thodi jaankari lekar expert ban gaya — adhura gyaan khatarnak hota hai.

literal_meaning: Hasty work is the devil's.
figurative_meaning: Rushing leads to mistakes; patience produces better results.
example: Jaldi mein sab gadbad kar diya — jaldi ka kaam shaitan ka.

literal_meaning: Big name, small sight.
figurative_meaning: Something or someone that is famous but disappointing in reality.
example: Itna sunaa tha restaurant ke baare mein, khana bekar tha — naam bade darshan chhote.

idiom: एक तो करेला ऊपर से नीम चढ़ा
literal_meaning: First bitter gourd, then topped with neem.
figurative_meaning: A bad situation made even worse by adding another negative element.
example: Pehle se pareshaan tha, ab yeh khabar bhi — ek toh karela upar se neem chadha.

literal_meaning: Remember your own deeds.
figurative_meaning: Be mindful of your own actions before judging others.
example: Doosron ko blame karne se pehle — apni karni yaad rakho.

literal_meaning: Time is very powerful.
figurative_meaning: Time changes everything; no situation is permanent.
example: Abhi bura lag raha hai, badlega — samay bada balvaan.

literal_meaning: What was in the mind stayed in the mind.
figurative_meaning: Failing to express one's feelings or desires; a wish left unfulfilled.
example: Woh kuch kehna chahta tha, nahi keh paya — man ki man mein rahi.

literal_meaning: Out of sight, out of mind.
figurative_meaning: Once someone leaves or is not visible, they are quickly forgotten.
example: Woh transfer hua aur sab bhool gaye — aankh ojhal pahad ojhal.

literal_meaning: What is greater — intelligence or a buffalo?
figurative_meaning: Brains are more valuable than brute strength or size.
example: Machine se nahi, dimag se kaam lena padega — akl badi ya bhains.

idiom: काठ की हाँडी बार बार नहीं चढ़ती
literal_meaning: A wooden pot cannot be placed on the fire again and again.
figurative_meaning: A trick or deception can only work once.
example: Ek baar chaal chali thi, ab nahi chalegi — kaath ki handi baar baar nahi chadhti.

literal_meaning: Diwali does not come every day.
figurative_meaning: Good times and celebrations do not last forever; enjoy them while they last.
example: Itna mat kharch karo, har roz Diwali nahi hoti.

literal_meaning: What moves is called a vehicle.
figurative_meaning: An active, functional person or thing has value; only those who work are respected.
example: Jo kaam karta hai wahi aage badhta hai — chalti ka naam gaadi.

idiom: एक मछली सारे तालाब को गंदा करती है
literal_meaning: One fish makes the entire pond dirty.
figurative_meaning: One bad person can corrupt an entire group.
example: Us ek aadmi ki wajah se poori team ka naam kharab hua — ek machli saare talab ko ganda karti hai.

idiom: जिसे पीना है वह कुएँ तक जाएगा
literal_meaning: The one who is thirsty will go to the well.
figurative_meaning: A truly motivated person will make the effort to get what they need.
example: Agar chahiye toh dhundh lega — jise peena hai woh kuen tak jayega.

idiom: बूँद बूँद से सागर बनता है
literal_meaning: Drop by drop, an ocean is formed.
figurative_meaning: Small consistent efforts accumulate into great results.
example: Roz thoda bachao — bund bund se saagar banta hai.

idiom: ठंडा लोहा गर्म लोहे को काटता है
literal_meaning: Cold iron cuts hot iron.
figurative_meaning: Calm and patience can overcome aggression and anger.
example: Usse ladna nahi, shaant raho — thanda loha garm lohe ko kaata hai.

idiom: बगल में छोरा, शहर में ढिंढोरा
literal_meaning: The child is in the armpit, yet the search is announced through the town.
figurative_meaning: Looking everywhere for something that is right beside you.
example: File laptop pe thi, poora daftar dhundha — bagal mein chhora, sheher mein dhindora.

idiom: हर काम का एक वक्त होता है
literal_meaning: Every task has its own time.
figurative_meaning: Everything should be done at the right moment; timing matters.
example: Abhi nahi, sahi waqt ka intezaar karo — har kaam ka ek waqt hota hai.

literal_meaning: A seer met by one-and-a-quarter seer.
figurative_meaning: Meeting your match; someone cleverer than the clever one.
example: Woh akad mein raha, phir usse bhi bada mila — ser ko sawa ser.

literal_meaning: If the end is good, everything is good.
figurative_meaning: A good outcome justifies the entire process; all's well that ends well.
example: Raasta mushkil tha par kaam hua — ant bhala toh sab bhala.

literal_meaning: If God is kind, even a donkey can become a wrestler.
figurative_meaning: With luck and favour on your side, even an incompetent person can succeed.
example: Vaoh kuch nahi karta, bas kismat achhi hai — khuda mehrban toh gadha pahalvan.

idiom: नौकर का नहीं यार का काम
literal_meaning: Not the servant's work, but a friend's work.
figurative_meaning: A true friend helps you without being asked and without payment.
example: Usne bina maange help ki — naukkar ka nahi yaar ka kaam.

idiom: इतना मत सोचो कि कुछ न हो
literal_meaning: Don't think so much that nothing gets done.
figurative_meaning: Overthinking leads to paralysis; sometimes action must replace analysis.
example: Plan baad mein, pehle shuru karo — itna mat socho ki kuch na ho.

idiom: सच्चा दोस्त वही जो मुसीबत में काम आए
literal_meaning: A true friend is one who is useful in trouble.
figurative_meaning: Real friendship is proven in difficult times, not easy ones.
example: Jab sab chale gaye woh ruka — sachcha dost wahi jo musibat mein kaam aaye.

idiom: आज का काम कल पर मत छोड़ो
literal_meaning: Do not leave today's work for tomorrow.
figurative_meaning: Procrastination leads to accumulation of problems.
example: Report aaj likhni thi, kal hogi nahi — aaj ka kaam kal par mat chhodo.

literal_meaning: Big talk leads to a bowed head.
figurative_meaning: Boasting leads to embarrassment when you fail to deliver.
example: Usne bahut dava kiya tha, ab sharminda hai — bade bol ka sir neeche.

idiom: हर पेड़ पर आम नहीं लगते
literal_meaning: Not every tree bears mangoes.
figurative_meaning: Not everyone you meet will be helpful or valuable.
example: Sab se expectation mat rakh — har ped par aam nahi lagte.

idiom: जो दिखता है वह बिकता है
literal_meaning: What is visible sells.
figurative_meaning: Presentation and visibility matter; things that are noticed get attention and value.
example: Marketing zaroori hai — jo dikhta hai woh bikta hai.

literal_meaning: Eating jaggery but avoiding the fried sweet made from it.
figurative_meaning: Accepting something while hypocritically rejecting something essentially the same.
example: Usne rishwat li par doosron ko daanta — gud khao gulgulon se parhej.

literal_meaning: Good days do come.
figurative_meaning: No matter how hard the current situation, better times will follow.
example: Himmat rakh — acchhe din aate hain.

literal_meaning: A frustrated cat scratches the pillar.
figurative_meaning: Taking out one's embarrassment or anger on an unrelated target.
